items.title: In pictures: Ascendance unveils full-scale ATEA hybrid-electric VTOL
items.summary:
French startup Ascendance unveiled the full-scale prototype of its ATEA hybrid-electric vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) aircraft on November 19, 2026, as the Toulouse-based company prepares for its flight-test campaign.

The unveiling follows the completion of the demonstrator’s airframe, which Ascendance announced on February 23, 2026. The structure was manufactured by Duqueine Group in Lyon, France, under Ascendance’s engineering direction, clearing the way for the integration of the propulsion system, avionics, and fly-by-wire flight controls.

Speaking to the media during the unveiling event, which took place at Muret-Lherm airfield near Toulouse, Ascendance co-founder Jean-Cristophe Lambert, highlighted also the strategic significance of the ATEA program, as the first European aircraft developed from scratch around a hybrid-electric architecture. Lambert referred to the need for Europe to strengthen its industrial autonomy in aerospace and defense and pointed out that the ATEA has been built mostly with European components and technology.

Ascendance has raised €60 million so far, a figure that Lambert acknowledged, is relatively small in comparison to the amounts raised by some eVTOL developers in the United States and China. This, however, has not prevented the French startup from making major progress to date, stated Lambert, taking pride in the efficient use of resources.

Ascendance expects the first flight of the ATEA prototype to take place at some point in early 2027, as soon as the company gets permission from the aviation authority to start its flight…
items.t: In pictures: Ascendance unveils full-scale ATEA hybrid-electric VTOL

items.title: Boeing Vs. Airbus Cockpits: How Yokes & Sidesticks Change The Way Pilots Fly
items.summary: Airbus and Boeing had the same technology available and reached opposite conclusions about what to do with it. The A320 introduced a digital fly-by-wire system to a commercial airliner for the first time, and with the mechanical linkage removed, a control column was no longer technically necessary. Airbus took that option and fitted a sidestick. Boeing arrived at fly-by-wire later with the 777 and 787, had no mechanical requirement for a yoke either, but kept one.
items.t: Boeing Vs. Airbus Cockpits: How Yokes & Sidesticks Change The Way Pilots Fly

items.title: US firms seek new 250-mile speed lane for supersonic-hypersonic flight tests
items.summary:
A group of US companies are looking to establish a new 250-mile speed corridor between Texas and New Mexico as a supersonic and hypersonic flight test facility.

On November 18, 2026, the four members, which includes two FAA -licensed spaceports, signed a letter of intent (LOI) to “jointly define, advocate for, and develop a dedicated high-speed flight test corridor”.

Midland Development Corporation, Midland International Air & Space Port, the New Mexico Spaceport Authority, operator of Spaceport America, and Starfighters Space said the “proposal comes as federal regulators consider easing overland supersonic flight restrictions and expanding US space launch capacity”.

The group argue that if successful, the 250-mile corridor between Midland International Air & Space Port in West Texas and Spaceport America in southern New Mexico could support repeatable, high-cadence supersonic and hypersonic flight research including sonic boom overpressure measurement and air traffic integration procedure development.

Spaceport America 

The test corridor would also provide real-world flight data to help shape evolving supersonic flight and space launch regulations.

“A long-term goal of the corridor is to one day support operations to and above the Kármán line for suborbital and orbital launch, air launch, point-to-point spaceflight, and the reentry and recovery of spaceflight vehicles and payloads,” the group added.

The LOI follows two federal actions now before the FAA. Firstly, a rulemaking for the removal of the longstanding prohibition on overland flight above Mach 1 with a…
items.t: US firms seek new 250-mile speed lane for supersonic-hypersonic flight tests

items.title: Inside Thales’ plan to keep Asia-Pacific’s fast-growing airline fleets airborne
items.summary:
With Asia-Pacific expected to remain one of the world’s fastest-growing aviation regions through 2050, Thales is betting that the airlines flying there will want two things from their maintenance partners. Firstly, that parts be close by and secondly, that those parts will be ready when needed.

Thomas Got, Managing Director of Aviation Global Services at Thales, spoke to AeroTime in an exclusive interview at the company’s booth during MRO Asia-Pacific 2026 in Singapore.

He described a strategy built on local presence, guaranteed parts availability and long-term partnerships, including a recent agreement with Vietjet.

Got, who was recently named a Knight of the National Order of Merit in France for his contributions to the defense and aerospace industries, has spent much of his career in those sectors, including work modernizing air surveillance and air defense systems.

He now oversees Thales’ aviation services business, where Asia-Pacific is a key growth market.

“The region is fast growing, probably the fastest-growing area worldwide,” Got said. “So for us, it’s very important to be well present in this market. It’s a question of bringing capabilities close to our customers.”

A three-hub footprint across Singapore, Beijing and New Delhi 

Thales runs its regional operations from a headquarters in Singapore, with additional sites in Beijing and New Delhi. The New Delhi facility, located near the city’s airport, opened in 2025.

Got explained the expansion reflects the company’s view that serving airlines in a region this large requires being physically present in its…
items.t: Inside Thales’ plan to keep Asia-Pacific’s fast-growing airline fleets airborne

items.title: Hanwha Systems wins first US contract for counter-drone radar
items.summary:
Hanwha Systems has secured its first radar export contract in the US, agreeing to supply short-range active electronically scanned array (AESA) radars to US defense technology company Rebellion Industries. 

The agreement is a pilot export deal, under which a small number of radars will initially be delivered to assess their suitability for the US market. Neither company disclosed the number of units ordered or the contract value. 

Hanwha said deliveries would take place in stages through early 2027. The two companies are also discussing follow-on contracts for larger orders in the US. 

Hanwha and Rebellion target US counter-drone market  

Under the agreement, Hanwha and Rebellion plan to integrate the South Korean company’s radar with Rebellion’s Sensor OS software to develop a counter-drone platform for military and civilian applications. 

According to Hanwha, the radars will initially be deployed at civilian infrastructure sites in the US, including oil refineries, corporate data centers, logistics centers and stadiums. 

Rebellion Industries, led by founder and CEO Shu Chowdhury, develops technology for detecting and responding to threats against critical infrastructure. Its product portfolio includes software that combines radar, electro-optical and other sensor data into a single operational picture, as well as its own compact AESA radar, called ARGUS. 

Compact AESA radar designed to detect low-flying drones  

The radar covered by the contract has a detection range of 10 kilometers (6.2 miles) and is designed primarily to detect and track drones and other small…
items.t: Hanwha Systems wins first US contract for counter-drone radar

items.title: F-35C completes first Ford-class carrier trials aboard John F. Kennedy
items.summary:
Two F-35C Lightning II fighters have completed the first launch and recovery trials aboard a Gerald R. Ford-class aircraft carrier, marking a step toward integrating the US Navy’s carrier-based stealth fighter with its newest warships.

The tests took place aboard the future USS John F. Kennedy (CVN 79), the second Ford-class carrier, over an 11-day period, Lockheed Martin announced on November 19, 2026.

According to the manufacturer, two F-35Cs from Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, completed 122 catapult launches and 122 arrested landings in 34 flights during the campaign.

The first F-35C arrested landing aboard Kennedy took place on October 13, 2026, coinciding with the US Navy’s 251st birthday. Lockheed Martin did not specify the start and end dates of the full test period.

Testing the F-35C with Ford-class launch and recovery systems 

Unlike the older Nimitz-class carriers, which use steam-powered catapults, Ford-class ships employ the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS) and Advanced Arresting Gear (AAG). These systems are designed to provide greater control over aircraft launches and recoveries.

The Ford class also features a redesigned flight deck and island, creating a different operating environment for aircraft and deck crews.

During the trials, engineers gathered data to verify the EMALS and AAG software and installations, assess the loads imposed on the F-35C during launches and landings, and validate the aircraft’s structural models.

The results will also support the development of aircraft launch and recovery bulletins, which…
items.t: F-35C completes first Ford-class carrier trials aboard John F. Kennedy

items.title: UK defense plan under fire as BAE Systems looks to cut 1,070 jobs
items.summary:
The UK’s defense plan has come under fire after British firm BAE Systems announced plans to cut 1,070 jobs, including 940 roles from within its air division.

The development comes as BAE Systems said it is looking to “reduce complexity, improve efficiency and ensure every pound invested delivers maximum value and capability back to defense”.

Following the announcement on November 18, 2026, the union Unite blamed delays in UK defense spending for “driving companies in the sector to make negative decisions impacting British jobs”.

“In order to stop the erosion of defense jobs and get the growth we need, the government needs to announce contracts for British built Typhoons and Collaborative Combat Aircraft immediately,” Unite General Secretary Sharon Graham said.

Edgewing 

In September 2025, Turkey ordered 20 Eurofighter Typhoon fighter jets from the UK, however this project is unlikely to sustain long-term job prospects.

On November 19, 2026, the Shadow Minister for Defence Procurement, Ben Obese-Jecty, said that if the Labour government does not support the industry with orders, then it “will simply go where the orders are”.

“The Government talks a good game on defense and resilience, but the reality doesn’t match rhetoric,” Obese-Jecty wrote. “As the rest of Europe rearms, the Government remains paralyzed by indecision.”

In a statement, BAE Systems said it had spoken with staff about the company’s “ongoing focus on enhancing our agility and competitiveness”.

“We are at an early stage in this process and will now enter into a period of consultation as we develop…
items.t: UK defense plan under fire as BAE Systems looks to cut 1,070 jobs

items.title: SITA’s Sumesh Patel on how Asia-Pacific airports can handle more with less space
items.summary:
Current predictions suggest that Asia-Pacific will account for almost half of the world’s future passenger growth – but its airports won’t be able to double in size to keep up. 

For SITA (Société Internationale de Télécommunications Aéronautiques), the solution lies in moving passengers, bags and borders through the same space more quickly, and in moving more of the airport journey away from the airport itself.

At Passenger Terminal Expo Asia 2026 in Singapore, AeroTime sat down with Sumesh Patel, President for Asia Pacific at SITA, the air transport IT provider, to discuss biometric borders, baggage tracking and how the region is preparing for a future of up to 10 billion passengers a year.

Patel said the timing of the expo’s first edition in Asia reflected where the industry is heading. “When we look at the airlines, the airports, the expansion – the future growth in terms of the passenger is in Asia,” he said, adding that the event had been busier than he expected.

Border Flow: from ‘stop and check’ to ‘walk through’ 

SITA launched its Border Flow lane as a commercial product on September 9, 2026, after trialing the concept for years at its customer experience center in Singapore.

The system pre-clears passengers before they reach the airport, enabling them to walk through border control without stopping. SITA claims to process travelers up to eight times faster than traditional e-gates, with 75% of travelers cleared before departure.

According to Patel, the benefits go both ways. Passengers no longer queue at gates or counters, while immigration officers can…
items.t: SITA’s Sumesh Patel on how Asia-Pacific airports can handle more with less space

items.title: Boeing 777X Pilots Have To Manually Extend The Wingtips Before Takeoff But Not Fold Up After Landing
items.summary: One of the Boeing 777X's most famous new features is its folding wingtips. They're roughly 11 feet (3.5 meters) wide each and are designed to be folded up whilst on the ground, allowing the aircraft to use the same airport facilities as older 777 models. They extend before takeoff and remain fully extended until after landing. Interestingly, it's the pilots' responsibility to extend the wingtips before takeoff, but the wingtips retract automatically after landing as the aircraft decelerates on the runway.
items.t: Boeing 777X Pilots Have To Manually Extend The Wingtips Before Takeoff But Not Fold Up After Landing

items.title: Belgium pledges 10 F-16s, France two Mirage jets for Ukraine by end of 2026
items.summary:
Ukraine’s allies announced plans to deliver 10 Belgian F-16 fighters and two French Mirage 2000-5F jets by the end of 2026, alongside additional air defense missiles, radars and ammunition, at the 37th meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group (UDCG). 

The commitments, published by Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense on November 18, 2026, followed a meeting at NATO headquarters in Brussels the day before. Several countries also pledged new funding for the Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) , through which allies finance US-made weapons for Kyiv. 

“This winter, our biggest priority is protecting the skies,” Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara said, according to the ministry. 

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who addressed the meeting remotely, called for the provision of 40 additional F-16 fighters . He said Ukraine’s existing jets spend considerable time undergoing maintenance and repairs, limiting their availability for combat missions. 

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius co-chaired the session. 

Defense ministers and representatives of Ukraine’s allies attend the 37th meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group at NATO headquarters in Brussels, Belgium. (Credit: NATO) 

UK, Germany and Nordic allies reinforce Ukraine’s air defenses 

The UK announced a £240 million (about $316 million) package that includes more than 1,000 short-range air defense missiles and launchers, along with more than a dozen radars. 

The missiles include Lightweight Multirole Missiles (LMM), manufactured by Thales in Belfast.…

items.title: Emirates’ new interim first-class lounge gives ‘taste of what’s to come’ at DXB
items.summary:
Emirates has opened a temporary first-class lounge at Dubai International Airport (DXB) before a series of major unveilings expected over the next few years.

On November 19, 2026, Emirates confirmed that the new lounge located at Concourse B, Terminal 3, will serve first-class customers for a year before pivoting into a next-generation business class lounge.

Tim Clark, President of Emirates airline, said that the new high-end lounge will give guests the “first taste of what’s to come” at DXB.

“If these are the lengths we will go to for a temporary lounge… just imagine what you can expect from new Emirates Lounges going forward,” Clark said.

Emirates 

According to the Dubai flag carrier, the newly unveiled lounge is part of an AED 400 million ($109 million) transformation, covering all its flagship lounges.

Emirates is undertaking an extensive two-year program to significantly elevate its lounge experience across Terminal 3. The interim first-class lounge in Concourse B represents the first step towards that ambition.

“Created as a luxurious temporary First-Class retreat while the wider refurbishment programme is ongoing, the lounge brings together contemporary elegance, comfort and functionality – in Emirates’ signature tones of gold, bronze, marble with accents of red,” Emirates explained.

The airline highlighted the lounge’s multipurpose seats with built-in chargers, footrests and tables, relax areas with chaise longue style daybeds, blankets, pillows and individual privacy.

There are also tables and dedicated workspaces that…

items.title: US Space Force taps France’s Eutelsat for military satellite links
items.summary:
Eutelsat Network Solutions, the US arm of French satellite operator Eutelsat, has secured a contract worth more than $60 million to provide military satellite communications to the US Space Force through its OneWeb constellation. 

The company announced the award on November 17, 2026, stating that the agreement would run for two years. 

It is part of Warrior Plans, a US Space Force initiative designed to give military units faster access to commercial satellite communications, particularly when operating in remote areas or environments where communications may be disrupted. 

OneWeb to provide military communications and navigation support  

Under the agreement, Eutelsat will provide access to its OneWeb low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite network, along with portable terminals that military personnel can deploy in the field. The contract also includes technical support and alternative positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) services, which could help military users maintain operations when conventional satellite navigation is unavailable or disrupted. 

Eutelsat did not specify how many terminals would be supplied, which military units would use the service, or what technology would underpin the alternative navigation capability. 

“Today’s military operations demand communications capabilities that are agile, resilient, and available anywhere in the world,” said Ian Canning, President and CEO of Eutelsat Network Solutions. 

US Space Force also turns to SpaceX’s Starshield  

The award follows earlier contracts issued by the US Space Force’s Commercial Satellite…
items.t: US Space Force taps France’s Eutelsat for military satellite links

items.title: Fire retardant caused corrosion in firefighting aircraft, NTSB finds
items.summary:
A fire retardant approved for use in US firefighting aircraft caused extensive corrosion during a single fire season, damaging wing structures, control cables, electrical connectors and engines, according to a National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) investigation.

The findings prompted the NTSB on November 17, 2026, to call for stronger US Forest Service testing requirements. Investigators found that the agency’s approval process had failed to adequately assess how the chemical would affect aircraft under actual operating conditions.

The retardant product, Fortress FR-200, manufactured by Fortress North America, was removed from the Forest Service’s approved list in December 2024. But the NTSB said withdrawing it and a related product did not address the shortcomings in the testing process that allowed them to be approved.

Corrosion reached primary wing structure 

The investigation involved two firefighting aircraft: a BAe 146-200A operated by Montana-based Neptune Aviation Services and an MD-87 operated by Oregon-based Aero Air, which flies firefighting missions as Erickson Aero Tanker.

Both participated in a 2023 Forest Service trial examining how the newly approved retardant could be used alongside an existing product.

The aircraft initially carried FR-200, which used magnesium chloride as its active retardant salt. Later in the season, they alternated between that product and Phos-Chek MVP-Fx, a phosphate-based retardant manufactured by Perimeter Solutions.

On the MD-87, corrosion penetrated more than half the thickness of a wing-spar doubler, a…
items.t: Fire retardant caused corrosion in firefighting aircraft, NTSB finds

items.title: Safety gaps persist after fatal Washington midair collision, report warns
items.summary:
Some safety weaknesses exposed by the collision between an American Airlines regional jet and a US Army helicopter near Washington, DC, remain nearly two years after the accident, according to a congressionally requested review released on November 18, 2026.

The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine called for stronger Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and Army safety oversight and recommended that Congress require a public assessment of safety and capacity before authorizing additional flights at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA).

The study builds on the National Transportation Safety Board’s (NTSB) investigation into the January 29, 2025, collision, which killed all 67 people aboard the two aircraft. It makes 25 recommendations covering airport operations, military flying and protection against midair collisions.

The review found that both the FAA and Army had failed to adequately recognize and address recurring collision risks before the accident.

The committee urged the FAA to spread flights more evenly throughout the hour to avoid bursts of traffic that strain controllers. It also called for a closer look at how airliners and helicopters share the airport’s busy airspace.

For military operations, the committee recommended standardized Washington-area airspace training and recurring proficiency checks. Assessments of routine training flights should also consider whether their objectives could be accomplished at another time, along another route, elsewhere or through simulation.

The review calls for faster completion of…
items.t: Safety gaps persist after fatal Washington midair collision, report warns

items.title: Russia opens investigation after An-12 military crash kills 19 in Siberia
items.summary:
Russian military investigators say they have opened a criminal investigation after an Antonov An-12 transport aircraft crashed near Kemerovo in southwestern Siberia on November 17, 2026, killing all 19 people aboard.

Russian media outlets reported that the aircraft had been flying from Novosibirsk to Kansk when one of its engines reportedly caught fire. The crew requested an emergency landing at Kemerovo Airport but crashed several miles short of the runway. Witnesses on the ground said the airplane was on fire before it crashed.

Russia’s Defense Ministry said the aircraft was conducting a routine flight when it went down in an unpopulated area near the village of Yagunovo. The ministry identified a “technical malfunction” as the preliminary explanation but did not specify what went wrong. A Russian Aerospace Forces commission is examining the accident.

The Investigative Committee said military investigators opened the case under Article 351 of Russia’s criminal code, which covers violations of flight rules or preparations for flight. Its announcement confirmed that all crew members and passengers died.

Kemerovo Governor Ilya Seredyuk visited the scene and said emergency crews had extinguished the fire. Authorities cordoned off the area and established an operations headquarters for investigators, rescue services and emergency medical personnel.

Investigators continued examining the crash site on November 18 and collecting evidence for forensic analysis, the newspaper reported.

Authorities have not publicly identified the victims or provided a confirmed breakdown of…
items.t: Russia opens investigation after An-12 military crash kills 19 in Siberia

items.title: Textron sells industrial arm for $1.2B to put aerospace and defense at its core
items.summary:
Textron has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its industrial arm for $1.2 billion, marking its future as a pure-play aerospace and defense company.

On November 18, 2026, the US firm confirmed that industrial outfits such as Kautex and Textron Specialized Vehicles businesses would be among those sold to a Kingswood Capital Management affiliate.

In April 2026, Textron announced its intent to separate its industrial segment to focus on its core franchises of Textron Aviation, Bell, and Textron Systems.

The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to required regulatory approval. Upon completion, the pure-play aerospace and defense company will be named New Textron.

Bell 

New Textron will include the Cessna and Beechcraft brands, military and commercial rotorcraft under the Bell brand and Textron Systems’ differentiated suite of aerospace and defense products and services.

“Today’s agreement is a defining milestone which will establish Textron as a premier, pure-play aerospace and defense company,” Lisa Atherton, CEO of Textron, said. “The sale of Industrial allows us to sharpen our strategic focus on growing our core A&D businesses while also returning capital to our shareholders.”

Atherton added: “I would like to thank all Industrial employees for their dedication and contributions over the years. Both Kautex and Textron Specialized Vehicles are leaders in their respective markets with iconic brands and talented teams.”

Under the New Textron brand, the company has over $12 billion in expected 2026 revenues and $19 billion in…
items.t: Textron sells industrial arm for $1.2B to put aerospace and defense at its core

items.title: Russian drone reportedly explodes near Antonov An-124 at Hostomel
items.summary:
A pro-Russian Telegram channel has published unverified footage that appears to show a Russian drone exploding close to an Antonov An-124-100M-150 inside a hangar at Hostomel Airport (GML), near Kyiv.  

The three-second clip was posted on November 18, 2026, by the channel Donbasskiy Partizan, which said a powerful explosion occurred near the aircraft in the former hangar of the An-225 Mriya. 

The aircraft, registered UR-82009, has been grounded at the airfield since it was damaged during the battle for the airport in February 2022. The extent of any additional damage remains unknown. 

An-124 stranded at Hostomel since the 2022 Russian assault  

UR-82009 was undergoing heavy maintenance at Hostomel, with its four engines removed, when Russian airborne troops assaulted the airfield on February 24, 2022. After Ukrainian forces retook the area in early April 2022, Antonov listed an An-124 among the aircraft damaged in the fighting, alongside the destroyed An-225. 

Footage recorded after the battle by Mriya pilot Dmytro Antonov showed the An-124 among the damaged aircraft. 

RELATED 

Mriya pilot Dmytro Antonov on Hostomel and the second An-225 [Part 1] 

Donbasskiy Partizan claimed that the aircraft had been undergoing preparations for a return to service for more than four years. However, AeroTime could not find a public statement from Antonov confirming a restoration program or setting out a timeline for the airframe. 

Antonov’s An-124 fleet also targeted in Germany  

Antonov Airlines has operated its An-124 fleet from Leipzig/Halle Airport (LEJ) in Germany since…
items.t: Russian drone reportedly explodes near Antonov An-124 at Hostomel

items.title: Founder of Vertical’s largest shareholder latest to join bolstered board
items.summary:
The founder of Vertical Aerospace’s largest shareholder Jason Mudrick has joined the company’s board of directors, taking a more prominent role moving forward.

On November 18, 2026, Mudrick, who founded Mudrick Capital Management , said it was time to “move from contributing behind the scenes to joining the Board”.

Mudrick Capital Management is a significant backer of Vertical Aerospace , having first invested in the electric vehicle and takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft developer around five years ago.

According to Vertical Aerospace, Mudrick Capital has provided close to $300 million of capital since its NYSE listing in 2021.

Five board member appointees since September 

Since September 2026, Vertical has appointed several high-profile individuals to its board in an effort to strengthen its expertise surrounding aerospace, defense, technology and capital markets.

Among them was former CEO of Airbus Commercial Aircraft, Fabrice Brégier, who became the new chair of Vertical.

Others included Marc Fontaine, who currently serves as CEO of Helsing SAS and the former CEO of Leonardo Helicopters US, Clyde M. Woltman.

Vertical said that Mudrick will bring “extensive experience in capital allocation, financing and strategic transactions, alongside a detailed understanding of Vertical and its strategy”.

Jason Mudrick (credit: Vertical Aerospace) 

“Mudrick Capital’s significant investment in Vertical reflects our belief in its technology, its people and the potential of electric aviation,” Mudrick said. “With a world-class Board now in place and important decisions for…

items.title: French-made fabric bottleneck complicates US Patriot missile ramp-up: WSJ
items.summary:
A little-known French-made fabric has become a potential stumbling block in the Pentagon’s plans to ramp up Patriot missile production, according to an investigation by the Wall Street Journal . 

The material, known as Raycarb C2B, is a carbonized rayon fabric used in the rocket motor of the PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (MSE) interceptor. ArianeGroup manufactures it and supplies it to Kansas-based Park Aerospace, which processes it into a heat-resistant composite used to protect rocket motor components. 

Park chairman and CEO Brian Shore told investors on October 8, 2026 , that the company was “sole-source qualified on the solid rocket motor for the PAC-3 MSE missile program” for the specialty materials it produces using ArianeGroup’s fabric. 

L3Harris builds the PAC-3 MSE’s solid rocket motor, while Lockheed Martin assembles the interceptor at its facility in Camden, Arkansas. 

How French rocket technology became critical to US missiles 

ArianeGroup’s manufacturing facility in Le Haillan, near Bordeaux, produces rocket motor nozzles for European launchers, including Ariane 6. (Credit: ArianeGroup) 

Raycarb C2B starts as rayon, a cellulose-based fiber historically used to reinforce tires. The fabric is heated in a controlled process that converts it into carbon cloth capable of withstanding extremely high temperatures. Impregnated with phenolic resin, it forms a composite that gradually erodes when exposed to intense heat, protecting the rocket motor structure underneath. 

Its origins go back to 1996, when Snecma Propulsion Solide, a predecessor of ArianeGroup,…
items.t: French-made fabric bottleneck complicates US Patriot missile ramp-up: WSJ

items.title: Aer Lingus to debut premium economy as part of long-haul fleet transformation
items.summary:
AIG-owned Aer Lingus will debut premium economy cabins for the first time ever as part of a major transformation of its long-haul fleet.

On November 18, 2026, Aer Lingus unveiled plans to refurbish 10 Airbus A330 widebody aircraft, describing the development as “one of the most significant investments” in “more than a decade”.

Under the plans, each of the 10 Airbus A330s will include business class, premium economy, and economy cabins with the first upgraded aircraft set to appear from October 1, 2027.

The first introduced A330 will serve select Dublin Airport (DUB) to John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) routes, namely EI104 and EI105.

Aer Lingus 

As more refurbished aircraft enter service, further North American routes will be added to the Aer Lingus schedule.

With new cabins, seating, dining and free Starlink inflight technology, along with the introduction of premium economy, Aer Lingus hopes to provide customers with a new way to fly transatlantic.

“This investment is much more than the introduction of a new cabin,” Lynne Embleton, CEO, Aer Lingus, said. “It is a transformation of the entire experience across our A330 fleet, elevating Business Class, Economy and, for the first time in Aer Lingus history, introducing Premium Economy.”

Embleton added: “Our ambition here is simple. We want to give our customers greater choice, comfort and connectivity, while creating an experience that feels unmistakably Aer Lingus.”

Premium economy details

items.t: Aer Lingus to debut premium economy as part of long-haul fleet transformation

items.title: Qantas Airbus A380 with Bluey, Bingo and friends design flies global in New Year
items.summary:
A Qantas Airbus A380 superjumbo featuring characters from the Bluey children’s animated TV series will take off globally in the New Year as part of a new collaboration between the airline and the program makers.

On November 18, 2026, Qantas unveiled the details behind its latest partnership, announcing that three aircraft will showcase designs featuring cartoon stars Bluey, Bingo and their friends.

The A380 design will see Long Dog on one side of the aircraft while Bluey, Bingo and three other characters will appear on the reverse side chasing after a red balloon.

Qantas 

And for those that cannot wait until the New Year, fear not as Qantas has come to the rescue with two Christmas inspired Bluey liveries and designs that will be flying over the holiday period.

The first Bluey artwork will appear on a QantasLink Dash-8 Q400, travelling across regional Australia, while the second will transform into a Bluey Qantas Freight Airbus A321, flying nationwide and to destinations across Asia and New Zealand.

The Bluey QantasLink Dash 8-Q400 features the title character and her younger sister alongside a huge pile of festive presents. The Qantas Freight Airbus A321 includes Bluey and her family with even more Christmas gifts.

And if you are worried about how to track the Bluey-themed planes, Qantas has also announced a dedicated tracker on its website.

items.title: US indicts Irish man over destruction of C-130H at Shannon Airport
items.summary:
US federal prosecutors have indicted an Irish man over an attack on a US Air National Guard C-130H Hercules at Shannon Airport (SNN) on April 11, 2026, saying the military transport aircraft was so extensively damaged that it will never fly again. 

The aircraft, valued at approximately $60 million, was rendered inoperable and effectively destroyed, according to the US Department of Justice (DOJ). Its tail section has since been removed by US authorities as part of efforts to store and dismantle the aircraft. 

The US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York announced on November 17, 2026, that Daithi O’Corrain, 48, also known as David Curran, faces one count of destruction of government property, which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison. O’Corrain is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. 

On April 12, 2026, AeroTime reported that the C-130 was expected to remain out of service pending assessment after video footage showed a man striking its wing and fuselage. The newly unsealed indictment provides further details about the damage inflicted inside the aircraft. 

How the C-130H was damaged from inside 

According to the indictment , O’Corrain breached the airport perimeter at approximately 04:39 local time and broke the locking mechanism on the aircraft’s rear crew door. The C-130H was parked on a taxiway, en route to another country on a US military assignment. 

Once inside, he allegedly barricaded himself in, securing the doors with straps, brackets and screws and placing ball bearings mixed with epoxy in the door tracks.

items.t: US indicts Irish man over destruction of C-130H at Shannon Airport

items.title: Beyond supplier discovery: Spacioply maps aerospace and space capabilities
items.summary:
Aerospace and space manufacturers may have more industrial capabilities available to them than they realize. The challenge extends beyond finding suppliers to understanding what capabilities exist, where they are located and how they compare.

For Sara Ghoneim, founder and CEO of Spacioply, this lack of visibility makes it difficult for manufacturers, governments and industry leaders to assess the strengths, maturity and gaps within industrial ecosystems.

Launched in April 2026, Spacioply is an aerospace and space capability intelligence platform designed to transform fragmented industrial information into structured, comparable and actionable intelligence. In an interview with AeroTime, Ghoneim explains how mapping and benchmarking global capabilities can support better industrial and strategic decisions.

From aircraft manufacturing to capability intelligence 

Ghoneim began her career as an industrial engineer at Boeing, working on commercial aircraft manufacturing. Her career subsequently expanded into supplier development, industrialization, supply chain strategy, program management, and the development of capabilities across industrial ecosystems. Working across these disciplines gave her different perspectives on the same challenge.

From the buyer’s perspective, organizations often rely on established supplier networks and familiar sources of information. From the supplier’s perspective, particularly among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), technical capabilities may remain largely unknown outside existing customers and geographical markets.

items.t: Beyond supplier discovery: Spacioply maps aerospace and space capabilities

items.title: US lawmakers reach aircraft safety deal after fatal Washington collision
items.summary:
US lawmakers reached an agreement in principle on November 17, 2026, to require civilian aircraft already subject to ADS-B Out rules to carry equipment that helps pilots identify nearby traffic, advancing aviation safety legislation prompted by the fatal collision between an American Airlines regional jet and a US Army helicopter near Washington, DC. 

Requirements for military aircraft remain unresolved.

Senators announced the agreement at a Capitol event organized by families of the victims. Republican Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas said he hoped Congress would pass the legislation before the end of the year.

The proposal centers on Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast In, or ADS-B In, which allows aircraft to receive information about surrounding traffic. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) already requires ADS-B Out, which broadcasts an aircraft’s position, in much of US controlled airspace. It does not require the complementary receiving equipment.

The proposed requirement would cover airliners, business aircraft and general aviation aircraft operating in airspace where the transmitting equipment is mandatory.

It would not impose a blanket equipment requirement on every aircraft. A vintage light airplane or hot-air balloon operating legally without ADS-B Out would not automatically have to install ADS-B In under the announced approach.

The Senate-passed ROTOR Act sets a December 31, 2031, equipage deadline and provides for lower-cost alternatives, including portable receivers, for aircraft with a maximum certificated takeoff weight below 12,500 pounds…
items.t: US lawmakers reach aircraft safety deal after fatal Washington collision

items.title: Germany’s AeroForce X surveillance aircraft completes maiden flight
items.summary:
Germany’s Aerodata has flown its AeroForce X surveillance aircraft for the first time, beginning flight tests of a design intended to be able to remain airborne for up to 40 hours.

The prototype completed its maiden flight from Strausberg Airport (SXB) in Brandenburg on November 14, 2026.

The aircraft carried a pilot for the test, although Aerodata is developing the aircraft for unmanned operations. Further piloted flights and autopilot testing will precede its first flight without a pilot.

Aerodata said the maiden flight assessed handling, stability and key systems, meeting all the objectives set for the test.

“Now, for the first time in the company’s history, we have flown our own aircraft platform,” Aerodata CEO Neset Tükenmez said.

The Braunschweig-based company has more than 40 years of experience developing aviation and reconnaissance systems. Its work includes equipment for maritime patrol, border surveillance and monitoring critical infrastructure. AeroForce X is intended to give the company an aircraft of its own to carry those systems.

Aerodata publicly unveiled the prototype at its Strausberg manufacturing site on August 19, 2026. With a wingspan of 26 meters, the aircraft is being developed as a medium-altitude, long-endurance unmanned aircraft system for military and security customers. Its intended missions include sustained surveillance of critical maritime infrastructure.

The company is targeting a payload capacity of up to 1.3 tonnes and endurance of up to 40 hours.

The aircraft’s modular design is intended to accommodate different reconnaissance…
items.t: Germany’s AeroForce X surveillance aircraft completes maiden flight

items.title: Controllers question official explanation for US air traffic control outage
items.summary:
Air traffic controllers and a former senior accident investigator are questioning the US government’s explanation for the November 13, 2026, communications failure that halted departures across the country for more than four hours .

Four days after the disruption, the controllers’ union says the FAA has yet to brief its workforce on the specific cause of the outage, and controllers say they want answers.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said it has traced the disruption to excessive data flooding its telecommunications network after contractor L3Harris installed a router at a remote radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas . A second router in Amarillo, Texas, also contributed to the instability, the agency said. Investigators are still determining why the problem spread to communications and radar feeds at 17 of its 22 en route control centers.

Gregory Feith, a former senior air safety investigator with the US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), questioned how the network could be vulnerable to such a widespread outage from a single computer router.

“Why is the air traffic control system vulnerable to a single-point failure? That doesn’t make any sense,” he told Denver television station 9NEWS .

Feith also challenged Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s emphasis on aging equipment and the transition from copper wiring to fiber-optic lines. He said modernization work had been underway for years and questioned why the existing network suddenly became unstable during Friday’s installation.

items.t: Controllers question official explanation for US air traffic control outage

items.title: Romania receives first two modernized IAR-99 jet trainers for F-16 pilots
items.summary:
Romania’s Ministry of National Defense (MApN) has accepted the first two of 10 IAR-99 SM jet trainers modernized by state-owned aircraft manufacturer Avioane Craiova. The aircraft were handed over in Craiova on November 16, 2026, more than two years after the original delivery deadline. 

The handover was confirmed in a statement issued by the ministry . The upgraded aircraft will support advanced jet training, particularly the transition to the F-16 fighter, while retaining a secondary close air support capability. 

They will be operated at the Air Force Application School “Aurel Vlaicu” in Boboc, where between 25 and 40 pilots are expected to undergo training annually in preparation for the F-16, depending on the number of graduates from the “Henri Coandă” Air Force Academy. 

IAR-99 modernization program faces delivery delays 

A Romanian Air Force IAR-99 Șoim jet trainer at the Avioane Craiova factory. (Credit: Romanian Government) 

The IAR-99 is a Romanian-designed, twin-seat subsonic jet trainer and light attack aircraft developed during the 1980s and manufactured by Avioane Craiova. The prototype made its first flight in December 1985, and the type entered Romanian Air Force service in 1988. 

A subsequent modernization produced the IAR-99 Șoim (Hawk), adapted for training pilots transitioning to the MiG-21 LanceR. 

The modernization to the SM (Standard Modernizat) configuration includes upgraded avionics, a new weapons system, and maintenance work to extend the airframes’ service lives. 

The contract, worth 275 million lei (approximately $57 million) excluding…
items.t: Romania receives first two modernized IAR-99 jet trainers for F-16 pilots
